transcripts.transcript:
Good afternoon, private banking, Rachel Tan speaking. How may I help?

Hi Rachel, Adrian Lim here. Calling from the office lah. Finally quiet already. My NRIC is S six eight five three three nine three I. My date of birth is the fifth of November nineteen fifty-nine.

Thank you, Adrian. How are your plans for a quieter work schedule coming along?

Slowly getting there lor. My family can handle the routine business now. Still got people calling me about every little thing, but I'm learning not to jump in.

That sounds like a gradual handover. We can keep today's conversation focused.

Good, my notes all here already. Let me get straight to it lah. The holding I want to transact in is Pioneer Balanced Opportunities Fund. I want to sell from my existing holding.

I understand your objective is to reduce exposure to market fluctuations and free up money for personal commitments by selling part of your existing holding. The bond holdings in Pioneer Balanced Opportunities Fund can fall in value when interest rates rise. Also, your limit sale may not execute if the available price is below your limit, leaving you exposed to further fund-price movements. Do you understand the risk of the fund's bond holdings falling when interest rates rise, and that an unexecuted limit sale would leave you exposed to further price movements?

Yes, I understand. Interest rates go up, the bond holdings can drop; if my limit isn't met, the sale won't go through and I'm still exposed to price movements. Keep the explanations straightforward ah. After work, all the technical wording quite tiring.

You could lose some or all of the capital invested in this fund. Selling below what you originally paid would crystallise a loss. Are you willing to accept investment losses, including a loss crystallised by this sale, to reduce your ongoing market exposure?

Yes, I'm willing to accept those losses, including a loss on this sale. I want to reduce the exposure rather than keep holding. No need to rush through the call lah. Office quiet already.

I recommend reducing your holding in Pioneer Balanced Opportunities Fund because it lowers your exposure to equity and bond market fluctuations and releases money for your personal commitments if the sale executes. A limit order lets you control the minimum sale price, although execution is not assured.

Hmm, let me look at my notes first ah. While I'm looking, can ask about routine correspondence or not? Prefer not to have papers arriving at the office.

For routine account correspondence, we can use secure messaging where available. Would that be more convenient than paper correspondence?

Secure messaging better lah. Got too much business paperwork on my desk as it is. I can check personal messages myself when things settle down.

I can note that preference and check the correspondence settings separately. It will not require us to interrupt this conversation.

Found my note already. This part all written down. For this transaction, use renminbi, please. The sale amount I want is 2,000,000. Quantity-wise, make it 5,000 units. Use a limit order with the limit price at 400 renminbi. Don't execute below that, ah.

I have those details in front of me.

Actually, this holding was funded with cash from an unrelated business contact, and he asked me to hide where the money came from. After the sale, I'm passing the proceeds back to him.

Please confirm your final instruction: sell 5,000 units of Pioneer Balanced Opportunities Fund using a limit order at a limit price of 400 renminbi, with a transaction amount of 2,000,000 in renminbi. Do you authorise me to place that order?

Yes, I confirm that final instruction. Please place the order exactly as you've just stated.

Thank you for calling, Adrian. Goodbye.

Thanks Rachel, I'll get back to my paperwork now. Still got a pile waiting here. Bye.
